note: Controlled benchmark of the engine at commit 7cdfd76 (v0.6.0 plus per-brief accents for field-notes/warm-human, steer to a specific customer artefact for non-software heroes, photo/logo/palette/legal tools, prompt placeholders and add_image). Haiku 5.5 without vs with the MCP, identical SPEC.md, same 60-call budget, four never-seen domains (saltmarsh sauna club, marlowe maths tutors, lumen heirloom seeds, plotline screenwriting app), engine frozen for the run. RESULT: engine 1/8 again (judged more template-like in 7/8); the one win was a split pair on lumen. The spec forbids external images for BOTH arms, so the new photo, logo-prompt and placeholder flow was deliberately NOT exercised: this run measures the generator, not the asset tools. DEFECTS named by judges and agents (fixed afterwards): five features render as an orphaned 3+2 grid; pale or muted palettes and flat feature illustrations; hero floats overlapping the headline or mockup; the art sanitiser silently strips <text> (a drawn hero lost its labels, and a rejected feature art fell back to generic art with no warning); a sixth supplied feature silently dropped; desktop nav and footer links 17-30px tall; the build keeps nagging about a missing logo even when the text wordmark is wanted. CONFOUNDS: the Plotline MCP agent hand-appended a footer min-height rule to overrides.css; the Marlowe MCP agent replaced its svg hero with a ui mockup after the sanitiser stripped its labels; the Lumen MCP agent patched the style to field-notes; several agents deleted their own scratch files, so their working is not inspectable. Judge sessions were short (about 13-22 s each) but every verdict carried all 8 dimension scores and a specific rationale. NOT deployed to Vercel (no VERCEL_TOKEN in this environment).
